english.title: Move / stop / operate an escalator / lift without authority on the Tyne and Wear Metro
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) whilst upon the Tyne and Wear Metro

(A)_[moved or attempted to move]_
(B)_[operated or attempted to operate]_
(C)_[stopped or attempted to stop]_

(D)_[an escalator, at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), other than in an emergency by means of equipment on or near which there was a notice indicating that it was intended to be used in an emergency]_
(E)_[a lift at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), other than in an emergency by means of equipment on or near which there was a notice indicating that it was intended to be used in an emergency]_
(F)_[a lift at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), other than by means of controls intended for the use of passengers]_
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 9(5) and 31(1) of the Tyne and Wear Metro Byelaws made under sections 58 and 62 of the Tyneside Metropolitan Railway Act 1973.

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 30 make provisions in relation to name and addresses.
(ii) Byelaw 31(2) provides powers for the removal of persons.
(iii) Byelaw 31(3) provides that when using these powers, an authorised person, including a constable, must show his/her identification if requested.
(iv) Byelaw 31(6) provides that in relation to this byelaw: An authorised person acting in the course of his duties shall not be liable for breach of this byelaw.
(vi Byelaw 31(4) provides that no person shall be subject to any penalty for breach of any of the Byelaws by disobeying a notice unless it is proved to the satisfaction of the Court before whom the complaint is laid that the notice referred to in the particular Byelaw was displayed.
(vi) Byelaw 31(5) provides that any person who attempts to breach this byelaw shall be liable to the same penalty as for the full offence.
